p: like the plague of leprosy: That it may be suspected to be leprosy.
deeper than the skin of his: That is, shrunken in, and be lower than the rest of the skin.
dark: As having the skin drawn together, or blackish.
unclean: Concerning his bodily disease: for his disease was not imputed to him for sin before God even though it were the punishment of sin.
clean that hath the plague: For it is not that contagious leprosy that infects, but a form of scales which does not leave the skin raw as leprosy does.
unclean: That is, declares that the flesh is not found, but is in danger of being leprous.
unclean: No one was exempted, but if the priest pronounced him unclean, he was put out from among the people: as appears by the example of Mary the prophetess, Nu 12:14 and by king Uzziah, 2Ch 26:20.
white bright spot: If he has a white spot in the place where the burning was and was later healed.
hair: Which was not wont to be there, or else smaller than in any other part of the body.
seek for yellow hair: He shall not care whether the yellow hair is there or not.
hair fallen off from the part: By sickness or any other inconvenience.
rent: In sign of sorrow and lamentation.
lip: Either in token of mourning, or for fear of infecting others.
skin: Whether it be garment, vessel, or instrument.
spread in the garment: But abide still in one place, as in Le 13:37.
colour: But remain as it did before.
whether it be bare within or: Or, whether it be in any bare place before, or behind.
the second time: So that he might be sure that the leprosy was departed, and that all opportunity for infection might be taken away.
